Time flows outward from the mark we make (part 3)
Learning to Swim
works.notes:
I use text, photography and assemblage and also make objects when I feel I need to.
I take ideas and concerns I have and  create a material response to
them. I try to create a response where the materiality speaks of the framework and
my response to it speaks of a response to that framework. The material response
does not describe its concerns but shows associations between the chosen forms
and leaves the viewer to decide.

I am occupied with how as individuals we function in existing structures: how the
codes of these systems effect how we see ourselves and how we define ourselves in
relation to them.

This work was initiated by my own experiences, the symbiotic effect of nurturing and
receiving and how that ties in with both learning and teaching. Whatever systems
you function in the individual relationships continue to create dialectical interventions
which will then alter framework by affecting the individuals within it.

The piece on show is called Learning to swim. The starting point for the piece is a
pair of worn leather boots.I wore these when I was pregnant with my son.
One boot is detached from its foot and attached to a constructed steel frame that
rocks. The inside of the boot is filled with feathers.
The companion boot is turned inside out and attached to another steel frame and
this is filled with bubble wrap.

There is a glazed clay object which is split into two, one half is pink and the other half
blue. This sits on a sheet of latex where one side is imprinted with the texture of the
steel from the tray. A yellow curtain cord attaches the clay objects to a spring high on
the wall.
The table structure is constructed of walnut, oak, ash and sycamore. The wood gets
lighter as it gets nearer the top. There is a glass panel which sits flush on the top and
has a hole in the centre. In the hole sits a blue cardboard NHS cardboard bowl
coloured with cobalt blue ink.

One of the leather pieces sits on a platform painted the same colour as the floor. The
other sits on fake grass. Attached to the platform is one piece of metal tubing with
brackets. The other leans against it and is supported by a nylon rod containing
another nylon rod covered in cellophane.

In the corner sitting on a plastic plant container lie three objects. One white spray
painted ceramic cone, an ink coloured piece of cardboard packaging and a flower
filled Lurex cone on a cake tray. This is the cone of flower power and the ceramic cone was first moulded into a shape and then punched to create the dent.

works.title: Catching a floating dream so it won’t fall from the sky
works.medium: silk, badminton racket, air dry clay, wire.
works.notes:
I read a news article about a bride to be who was left at the alter. She threw herself off the top of her apartment block wearing her wedding dress. 
I imagined a net with wings that could fly up and save her.

works.title: speaking with a voice from a place not here.
Memento mori
works.notes:
The phrase is Roman. Used as a way of seeing that things are temporary.
A practice called 'Negative visualisation'. spend time imagining losing the things you value.The discomfort in building something that matters. grief from loving beings that are mortal. It is a sign of life. To live is to experience this loss. having to suffer.
In having suffered the search for something deeper happens. ‘Samvega', a Sanskrit word meaning 'collected speed'. An impulse to spurn the material concerns of every day life to search for something deeper.

bio.text:
Am still here. Making, shaping and doing. Life gives us oranges and we make lemon juice. 
Things shift, we change and timelines move.
I am a now living on the West coast of Ireland. Looking at the same horizon. Different vantage
point. Please connect. It would be great to hear from you. Contact: cerlin@live.com
bio.statement: I am concerned with what it means to dwell, not as a singular notion which exists in given concepts but something more haphazard. A juncture where collisions happen when emotional, personal, social and political meet. I use materialsI I have in my space as well as paint, photography, assemblage, text and also make things. I like to repurpose materials that have a history. Maybe the empirical has only discovered a fraction of what we can explain. What we believe and can’t prove will slowly reveal itself as we open up the boundaries of investigation.
